requirements.title: A VALUE statement has an optional double colon and a required dummy-name list
requirements.definition: VALUE is followed by an optional double colon and a nonempty comma-separated dummy-arg-name list. R401 supplies the list; explicit R1534/C1571 supplies a name of a real dummy argument, overriding assumed R402. C867 further restricts VALUE to eligible dummy data objects, not dummy procedures or procedure pointers. Array/coarray specifications, selected subobjects and invocations are not part of this name list.

pending.double-colon-form: PENDING compile/positive-control under a qualified F2023 profile: a complete module contains subroutine s(x), with IMPLICIT NONE, prior INTEGER :: x, a single VALUE :: x statement, no other VALUE specification, no conflicting attributes and no body reference or call. x is an ordinary scalar data dummy. The module procedure provides an explicit interface; statement admission is not a value-copy or invocation observation.
pending.no-double-colon-form: PENDING the same complete ordinary data-dummy context with VALUE x instead. Omit both colons together. Retain the dummy header, type, absence of conflicting attributes and no other VALUE specification. Chosen prior typing is an isolation technique, not a universal ordering requirement.
pending.multiple-data-dummies: PENDING compile/positive-control: a complete module procedure s(x,y) declares distinct ordinary INTEGER dummies x,y and has VALUE :: x,y once. Both actual formal identities and their types are established; there is no INTENT(OUT/INOUT), POINTER, ALLOCATABLE, VOLATILE, coarray or assumed-size/rank complication. No missing-provider or call failure can stand in for list admission.
pending.required-name-list: PENDING separate diagnostic/control pairs with VALUE alone and VALUE :: alone in the complete s(x) specification part. Insert only the already declared eligible x, including required token separation, for each control. Keep a correct procedure ending and no duplicate VALUE attribute. Require a missing-list cause, not generic EOF, wrong dummy role or unsupported VALUE.
pending.single-colon-repair: PENDING one-predicate diagnostic/control: VALUE : x in that same valid dummy context, repaired only by inserting the second colon. The single colon is not an optional-double-colon alternative. Type, role, interface and all other attributes remain fixed; reporting need not be fatal or print R864.
pending.list-separator-repairs: PENDING separately isolated missing-comma and trailing-comma variants for the complete two-dummy x,y context. Insert or remove only the offending comma. Repeating a name or giving VALUE in both a type declaration and a statement would activate C815 and is not the intended grammar contrast.
pending.name-not-designator: PENDING diagnostic/control in an ordinary non-BIND module subroutine with an explicit-shape INTEGER dummy a(2): VALUE :: a(1), repaired only to VALUE :: a. C867 does not ban every ordinary array, but assumed-size and assumed-rank contexts are excluded. A separately qualified box%field contrast needs a complete accessible simple derived data dummy and a whole-box repair without coarray potential subobjects or other incompatible attributes. The selected subobject is not another R1534 name.
pending.dummy-name-and-eligibility-source: PENDING finite source/interface graph R864 -> R401 -> R1534/C1571, then C867 and related declaration constraints. Bind the live statement/name spans to actual formal declarations and verify the VALUE attribute origin. An ordinary dummy procedure or procedure pointer fails the data-object condition; a nondummy can also violate C1571. Assumed-type, assumed-rank, coarray and coarray-potential-subobject premises remain with their actual owners. Do not create a supposedly isolated local syntax diagnostic from a wrong entity category.
pending.attribute-combinations-and-interoperabil: PENDING finite C868/C869 and18.3.7 relationships. VALUE with INTENT(IN) or no INTENT is distinct from the forbidden ALLOCATABLE/POINTER/VOLATILE/OUT/INOUT combinations. OPTIONAL plus VALUE is prohibited for a BIND procedure, not universally for non-BIND procedures; absent-use rules still apply. Any BIND(C) scalar INTEGER(C_INT) context must import the actual guaranteed C_INT and satisfy all interface/prototype conditions. Ordinary Fortran array or derived VALUE admission is not a universal C ABI, descriptor, kind, layout or companion-call witness. Existing C interoperation programs retain their owners and profiles.
pending.anonymous-object-and-component-source: PENDING canonical source/operation relationship to15.5.2.4p4/p6/note2,15.5.2.5 and7.5.8, not a new local S effect. A future scalar parent can use a defined INTEGER actual7 and a genuine VALUE formal with no INTENT, observe its local change to11 and separately the caller value7. A future simple derived parent must distinguish a copied ordinary component from a pointer component's retained association to a defined live target: target mutation can be visible without changing the actual object's pointer association or ordinary component value. No alias/other-argument restriction is waived. Allocation-state/component, type/kind/rank/parameter and TARGET+VALUE pointer-lifetime cases need their full canonical premises; never query a pointer to the anonymous dummy after its lifetime ends. A physical copy, stack address, destructor callback or universal deep copy is not the oracle.
pending.scope-order-and-existing-owner-source: PENDING exact8.1/8.2/8.5.1 and procedure/scope relationships. Neither VALUE on a name nor prior local typing manufactures a formal argument. C1107 forbids a VALUE statement in BLOCK;14.2.2p9 supplies no VALUE exception for USE-associated entities. The selected controls use actual local formals. A proposed host-associated confirmation or re-attribution must separately resolve the existing dummy/attribute identity under19.5.1.4, rather than assume either a blanket permission or a blanket prohibition. A standalone VALUE statement and a VALUE type attribute in the same scoping unit are not a valid duplicate control. Preserve every existing case/owner/role; any future canonical witness needs an actual complete input and supported relation contract, not keyword matching, a clone or automatic numbered-target credit.

requirements.oracle: Complete ordinary program-unit compile admissions and source-minimal grammar report/control pairs, with actual dummy identity, supported types and compatible attributes already valid. Source/interface plans require bound statement origins, formal declarations and canonical-owner evidence. Canonical invocation effects remain separately pending; no case or relation is implemented here.
requirements.oracle_limitation: 4.2 requires a capability to detect and report numbered violations, not mandatory fatal rejection, a nonzero status, a particular English message or printed R864. Generic keyword/expected-token text, wrong type/role, duplicate attributes, missing providers, unsupported features, source echoes, crashes and resource errors are not corroboration. Syntax acceptance is not anonymous-object, component, ABI or runtime evidence. No compiler run, local no-op S classifier, approval or automatic source-use/link credit is supplied.

accounting.rationale: Nonempty list under R401 and explicit dummy-arg-name under R1534/C1571. The complete502-head original scan identifies that explicit production, not an assumed R402 replacement. C867/C868/C869 retain their separate predicates.

Normative statement-to-VALUE attribute route for the listed dummy arguments, with the exact8.5.19 reference. The canonical anonymous effective-object and component-value meanings are not duplicated as a local S or no-op program. All proposed source/interface/operation evidence remains pending.

A separate attribute specification statement is allowed under8.5.1. Its live source occurrence must be distinguished from VALUE in a type declaration or another statement context; it is not itself a procedure invocation or executable copy operation.

VALUE specifies an argument-association category, not a compulsory machine calling convention. PENDING finite association/source relationships to15.5.2.4/.5, including a definable anonymous effective object for a present VALUE dummy, lawful actual values and component semantics.

Only listed, eligible data dummies receive the attribute by this route. A formal name alone is insufficient for C867's data category, and names not in the list do not gain VALUE. Complete type/rank/interface/scope conditions precede any admission or call observation.

8.5.19/C867-C869,15.5.2.4/.5,7.5.8 and18.3.7 retain the actual eligibility, anonymous-object, component and interoperability owners. Preserve existing C interoperation, derived-value, argument and other cases/links without retagging, cloning or new positive-control opt-ins. No mechanism is implemented.

review_rationale: Independent complete original primary source and bounded canonical-dependency review a3a97c7e83c474fa523bddf2dcbefe8f6ce805be70e7364c7da467b2d1df25a9, registered in doc/source_audits/batch_077.json. R864 has optional double colons and a required R401 list using explicit R1534/C1571, not assumed R402. Actual VALUE data-dummy eligibility under C867, the distinct C839 assumed-rank exclusion, C868 incompatible entity attributes and conditional BIND/OPTIONAL C869 retain their canonical owners. Ordinary non-BIND explicit-shape arrays are not universally excluded, and pointer components are not the dummy entity's POINTER attribute. Present VALUE means an anonymous definable effective object under15.5.2.4p4/p6, not physical-copy, deep-copy, ABI or callback strategy. Component association, alias rules, TARGET+VALUE pointer lifetime, actual interfaces, presence and four-piece C interoperability remain gated. C_INT is supported under18.2.2p3, not a guessed kind number. BLOCK/USE restrictions and the host-associated VALUE identity lead remain exact. All11facets stay pending; p1 is an attribute-route definition, not a local S effect.
